margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Company adjusted EBITDA margin on total revenue, same basis as VA consensus EBITDA over revenue (FY2025 company 11.1% vs VA 11.06%). The framing is a standing annual rate of 10 to 20 bps a year, guided for full year 2026 and 'over the longer term', with no end year or level. The CFO says it has been the commitment for a decade.

statements.quote: we remain well-positioned to achieve our target of 10-20 basis points adjusted EBITDA margin expansion for the full year, as well as over the longer term. We have committed to this level of margin expansion over the last decade, during which we have averaged more than 10 basis points per year

street.gap_assumption: Calendar fiscal year, so Baba FY labels equal company years. FY2026 target = FY2025 actual 11.1% plus the 15 bps midpoint = 11.25% vs consensus 11.23% (+2 bps). Extending 15 bps a year to FY2028 gives 11.55% vs consensus 11.62% (-7 bps). The street already models the full 10 to 20 bps a year path (+17, +14, +25 bps).
street.source: Baba data_financials fundamentals (Visible Alpha consensus), fetched 2026-10-02

evidence_of_progress.note: Q1 2026 adj EBITDA margin 11.2% vs 11.3% (-14 bps on VA actuals; company called it stable); Q2 2026 11.2%, +10 bps YoY per CFO (doc 130283). Revenue flat YoY in Q2 ($474.5M); federal -9.5%, non-federal +6.6%. LTM 11.06% (Q3 2025 to Q2 2026; Q2 2026 from the call because VA still carries an estimate).

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: the 10 to 20 bps a year framing implies 11.25% for FY2026 vs 11.23% consensus (+2 bps) and about 11.55% for FY2028 vs 11.62% consensus (-7 bps). The only leadership change is an internal reshuffle (Morgan COO/CFO, Choate President) under a 7-year CEO.
verdict: Down 52% and cheap with an internal CFO and President reshuffle, but the decade-old 10 to 20 bps a year margin goal is already in consensus; nothing for the street to underwrite.
open_questions: Is Choate's appointment as President a CEO succession step, and would a new CEO reset the margin framework?
Can ERP and AI back-office savings lift the rate above 20 bps a year, or does management keep reinvesting the excess?
Does a commercial energy acquisition change the margin mix enough to matter?
